storyPrompt: Write a quiet English story about checking a disputed delivery before a public demonstration. Orla is a practical conservator. Dex is an assistant who is allowed to disagree. Mina keeps the public records. The story takes place at the seed library. The seed tin must remain intact. No character may be physically injured. Keep practical actions precise. Use third-person past tense centred on Orla. Plan six chapters, each targeting 750 words. No earlier book or borrowed fictional world is assumed.

chapters.purpose: Orla reads the handling note and asks Mina about the missing page.
chapters.turn: Mina supplies a duplicate page; the team agrees to continue checking before a demonstration.

chapters.title: The Copy
chapters.purpose: Orla compares the duplicate with a pencil copy.
chapters.turn: Dex identifies a transposed line and they agree on a corrected label.

chapters.title: Demonstration
chapters.purpose: The team prepares the public demonstration at the seed library.
chapters.turn: Orla credits Dex for finding the error, without claiming the item was lost.

chapters.title: Storage
chapters.purpose: Orla completes the demonstration and files the corrected loan register.
chapters.turn: The intact seed tin is stored securely and the dispute is closed.

texts:
Orla received the sealed seed tin and checked its outer label. The seed library was open, though there were no visitors at the table. Orla cleared a space before setting anything down. Dex moved the loose tools to a tray and waited for instructions. Neither of them treated a late delivery as proof of a lost object. They checked what they could see and left a blank beside what they could not yet establish.

The work required a little patience. A faded number was difficult to distinguish from a stain, so Orla turned the sheet towards the window rather than writing over it. Dex read the number aloud. They compared their readings, found that they agreed, and entered it only once. The seed tin remained intact on the cleared table throughout the check.

Orla made a short note of the work completed that day. The note separated observation from intention: a task written for tomorrow did not become a task already done. Dex asked whether the uncertainty meant they should abandon the demonstration. Orla said that an unanswered question was a reason to check, rather than a reason to invent an answer. It was an ordinary distinction, but making it aloud helped them continue without blaming anyone.

Orla noticed a red seam but left it unopened. They put the tools back in the tray. Orla recorded that result and closed the current work period. The next planned task remained unwritten in the story. No one had opened a different room, visited another site, or completed the later demonstration in the interval between these actions.
